summary: Sangyeob Cha is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at Dongguk University (2001–2008). Cha served as HK Professor at Geumgang University (2011–2022) and as a researcher at Kyungpook National University in 2020.

Sanit Sinak specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned degrees from Mahamakut Buddhist University, Ramkhamhaeng University, and Silpakorn University, and served as an instructor at Mahamakut Buddhist University in 2014.

Sanjay Shakya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Tribhuvan University (2008–2009) and was appointed assistant professor at Lumbini Buddhist University in 2024.

Sanjay Subrahmanyam is a historian educated at St. Stephen's College and the Delhi School of Economics. His career includes professorships at Oxford, the EHESS, UCLA—where he was founding director—and the Collège de France (2013–2021).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under M. K. Ganguli and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta is an Indologist who earned doctorates from Visva-Bharati and Utrecht under Jan Gonda. She held posts at Jadavpur, Visva-Bharati, and Calcutta, before serving at Utrecht University (~1968–1986) and the University of Oxford (~1986–2005).

Sanjukta Poddar works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed an MA and PhD at the University of Chicago (2015–2022), where she was a postdoctoral fellow (2022), before joining Leiden University as assistant professor in 2023.

Sanne Dokter-Mersch specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi, continuing there as a postdoctoral researcher in 2022.

Santanu Sarkar works in Indology. He studied at the University of North Bengal, Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University, Burdwan University, and IIT Kharagpur (PhD, 2020–2026), becoming an assistant professor at the University of Engineering & Management in 2026.

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhaddanta Narada and at Harvard University. He taught at Rangoon University, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised Myanmar's Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Sara Frumento is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She studied for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at Wolfson College, University of Oxford, where she also holds an academic post.

Sara Grant was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar educated at Oxford and Mumbai under Richard De Smet. She taught at Sophia College (~1957–1972) and Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth (~1972–1995), and co-led the Christa Prema Seva Ashram.

Sara L. McClintock, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, completed her PhD at Harvard (2002) under Tom Tillemans. She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003) and became an associate professor at Emory University (attested 2026).

Sarah Aoife Richardson works in history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto (2016) under Jenny Purtle, having also studied under John C. and Susan L. Huntington, Dina Bangdel, and others.

Sarah Cymbal is a scholar of history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University of Culture and Arts and Russian-Armenian University, where she holds a post while directing a Silk Road research centre.

Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar of art history, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Michigan and Kobe. She served as associate professor at Northwestern University (1996) and directrice d'études at the EPHE (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale and completed her PhD at the University of Virginia (1999–2007), later holding posts at Columbia and Northwestern University.

Sarah Harding is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Lama Tenpa. She served on the faculty at Naropa University (~1992–2018) and became a fellow of the Tsadra Foundation around 2000.

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Tübingen and held an affiliation there (attested 2026).
